Please check typos.path in Settings.`\n         );\n       }\n     );\n   }\n \n   //if (config.package.releaseTag === null) return \"typos-lsp\";\n \n   const ext = process.platform === \"win32\" ? \".exe\" : \"\";\n   const bundled = vscode.Uri.joinPath(\n     context.extensionUri,\n     \"bundled\",\n     `typos-lsp${ext}`\n   );\n \n   return await vscode.workspace.fs.stat(bundled).then(\n     () => bundled.fsPath,\n     () => {\n       throw new Error(\n         \"Unfortunately we don't ship binaries for your platform yet. \" +\n           \"Try specifying typos.path in Settings. \" +\n           \"Or raise an issue [here](https://github.com/tekumara/typos-lsp/issues) \" +\n           \"to request a binary for your platform.\"\n       );\n     }\n   );\n }\n \n export function deactivate(): Thenable<void> | undefined {\n   if (!client) {\n     return undefined;\n   }\n   return client.stop();\n }\n \n"},"toolTelemetry":{"properties":{"command":"view","options":"{\"truncateBasedOn\":\"tokenCount\",\"truncateStyle\":\"middle\"}","inputs":"[\"path\",\"command\"]","resolvedPathAgainstCwd":"false","fileExtension":"[\".ts\"]","viewType":"file"},"metrics":{"resultLength":5063,"resultForLlmLength":5063,"responseTokenLimit":234000},"restrictedProperties":{}}},"id":"c3775819-9c60-4335-850e-6a4cbe1f730a","timestamp":"2026-06-21T20:04:53.358Z","parentId":"2cb57f69-c99b-4cc2-914a-e9c28234c78a"}

Specifically, the client now uses `LogOutputChannel` for its output and trace channels instead of the standard VSCode `OutputChannel` type. {"type":"tool.execution_complete","data":{"toolCallId":"call_MHw0MUI4NmhaaGlxZmswNXpYQTg","model":"gemini-3.5-flash","interactionId":"58a73426-9394-4fd9-be34-f2848c63a77d","turnId":"15","success":true,"result":{"content":"{\"type\":\"output_text\",\"text\":{\"value\":\"Here's some context and guidance regarding the `LogOutputChannel` in the context of `vscode-languageclient` version 9.0.0:\\n\\n## `vscode-languageclient` and Logging\\n\\n- The `vscode-languageclient` library is the official Language Server Protocol (LSP) client for Visual Studio Code extensions. It provides utilities to connect VS Code to language servers.\\n- Logging is a core part of developing, debugging, and maintaining LSP extensions.\\n- The `LogOutputChannel` is an interface representing an output channel specifically for logging, as defined in more recent versions of the `vscode` and `vscode-languageclient` APIs.\\n\\n## Using `LogOutputChannel` in `vscode-languageclient@9.0.0`\\n\\n**As of version 9.0.0:**\\n\\n- The `LogOutputChannel` is available as part of the VS Code API (`vscode.LogOutputChannel`), which can be used for structured logging. \\n- `vscode-languageclient` version 9.0.0 supports passing your own `LogOutputChannel` into options for enhanced LSP logging.\\n\\n### Example Usage\\n\\nYou can create a log output channel and use it within your language client’s options:\\n\\n```typescript\\nimport * as vscode from 'vscode';\\nimport { LanguageClient, LanguageClientOptions, ServerOptions } from 'vscode-languageclient/node';\\n\\n// Create a log output channel\\nconst logChannel: vscode.LogOutputChannel = vscode.window.createOutputChannel('LSP Logs', { log: true });\\n\\nconst clientOptions: LanguageClientOptions = {\\n  // ...other options,\\n  outputChannel: logChannel, // For user-facing logs\\n  // Optionally, provide logOutputChannel for protocol logs\\n  logOutputChannel: logChannel, // For protocol/log output (newer pattern)\\n};\\n\\nconst serverOptions: ServerOptions = {...};\\n\\nconst client = new LanguageClient(\\n  'myLanguageServer',\\n  'My Language Server',\\n  serverOptions,\\n  clientOptions\\n);\\nclient.start();\\n```\\n\\n### Notes\\n\\n- Prior to VS Code extension API v1.56.0, there was just `OutputChannel`. The `LogOutputChannel` adds log levels and is intended for logging vs transient output.\\n- Using `LogOutputChannel` enables better log granularity and can be filtered by level (info, warn, error).\\n- Be sure your extension's `engines.vscode` in `package.json` is set to a VS Code version that supports `LogOutputChannel` (>=1.56.0).\\n\\n## Further Reference\\n- [VS Code API Output Channels](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#window.createOutputChannel)\\n- [vscode-languageclient Changelog](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/blob/main/client/CHANGELOG.md)\\n\\nIf you provide more details on your use-case (e.g., code, error messages, or specific goals), I can offer more targeted help!\",\"annotations\":null},\"bing_searches\":null,\"annotations\":null}","detailedContent":"{\"type\":\"output_text\",\"text\":{\"value\":\"Here's some context and guidance regarding the `LogOutputChannel` in the context of `vscode-languageclient` version 9.0.0:\\n\\n## `vscode-languageclient` and Logging\\n\\n- The `vscode-languageclient` library is the official Language Server Protocol (LSP) client for Visual Studio Code extensions. It provides utilities to connect VS Code to language servers.\\n- Logging is a core part of developing, debugging, and maintaining LSP extensions.\\n- The `LogOutputChannel` is an interface representing an output channel specifically for logging, as defined in more recent versions of the `vscode` and `vscode-languageclient` APIs.\\n\\n## Using `LogOutputChannel` in `vscode-languageclient@9.0.0`\\n\\n**As of version 9.0.0:**\\n\\n- The `LogOutputChannel` is available as part of the VS Code API (`vscode.LogOutputChannel`), which can be used for structured logging. \\n- `vscode-languageclient` version 9.0.0 supports passing your own `LogOutputChannel` into options for enhanced LSP logging.\\n\\n### Example Usage\\n\\nYou can create a log output channel and use it within your language client’s options:\\n\\n```typescript\\nimport * as vscode from 'vscode';\\nimport { LanguageClient, LanguageClientOptions, ServerOptions } from 'vscode-languageclient/node';\\n\\n// Create a log output channel\\nconst logChannel: vscode.LogOutputChannel = vscode.window.createOutputChannel('LSP Logs', { log: true });\\n\\nconst clientOptions: LanguageClientOptions = {\\n  // ...other options,\\n  outputChannel: logChannel, // For user-facing logs\\n  // Optionally, provide logOutputChannel for protocol logs\\n  logOutputChannel: logChannel, // For protocol/log output (newer pattern)\\n};\\n\\nconst serverOptions: ServerOptions = {...};\\n\\nconst client = new LanguageClient(\\n  'myLanguageServer',\\n  'My Language Server',\\n  serverOptions,\\n  clientOptions\\n);\\nclient.start();\\n```\\n\\n### Notes\\n\\n- Prior to VS Code extension API v1.56.0, there was just `OutputChannel`. The `LogOutputChannel` adds log levels and is intended for logging vs transient output.\\n- Using `LogOutputChannel` enables better log granularity and can be filtered by level (info, warn, error).\\n- Be sure your extension's `engines.vscode` in `package.json` is set to a VS Code version that supports `LogOutputChannel` (>=1.56.0).\\n\\n## Further Reference\\n- [VS Code API Output Channels](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#window.createOutputChannel)\\n- [vscode-languageclient Changelog](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/blob/main/client/CHANGELOG.md)\\n\\nIf you provide more details on your use-case (e.g., code, error messages, or specific goals), I can offer more targeted help!\",\"annotations\":null},\"bing_searches\":null,\"annotations\":null}","contents":[{"type":"text","text":"{\n  \"type\": \"output_text\",\n  \"text\": {\n    \"value\": \"Here's some context and guidance regarding the `LogOutputChannel` in the context of `vscode-languageclient` version 9.0.0:\\n\\n## `vscode-languageclient` and Logging\\n\\n- The `vscode-languageclient` library is the official Language Server Protocol (LSP) client for Visual Studio Code extensions. It provides utilities to connect VS Code to language servers.\\n- Logging is a core part of developing, debugging, and maintaining LSP extensions.\\n- The `LogOutputChannel` is an interface representing an output channel specifically for logging, as defined in more recent versions of the `vscode` and `vscode-languageclient` APIs.\\n\\n## Using `LogOutputChannel` in `vscode-languageclient@9.0.0`\\n\\n**As of version 9.0.0:**\\n\\n- The `LogOutputChannel` is available as part of the VS Code API (`vscode.LogOutputChannel`), which can be used for structured logging. \\n- `vscode-languageclient` version 9.0.0 supports passing your own `LogOutputChannel` into options for enhanced LSP logging.\\n\\n### Example Usage\\n\\nYou can create a log output channel and use it within your language client’s options:\\n\\n```typescript\\nimport * as vscode from 'vscode';\\nimport { LanguageClient, LanguageClientOptions, ServerOptions } from 'vscode-languageclient/node';\\n\\n// Create a log output channel\\nconst logChannel: vscode.LogOutputChannel = vscode.window.createOutputChannel('LSP Logs', { log: true });\\n\\nconst clientOptions: LanguageClientOptions = {\\n  // ...other options,\\n  outputChannel: logChannel, // For user-facing logs\\n  // Optionally, provide logOutputChannel for protocol logs\\n  logOutputChannel: logChannel, // For protocol/log output (newer pattern)\\n};\\n\\nconst serverOptions: ServerOptions = {...};\\n\\nconst client = new LanguageClient(\\n  'myLanguageServer',\\n  'My Language Server',\\n  serverOptions,\\n  clientOptions\\n);\\nclient.start();\\n```\\n\\n### Notes\\n\\n- Prior to VS Code extension API v1.56.0, there was just `OutputChannel`. The `LogOutputChannel` adds log levels and is intended for logging vs transient output.\\n- Using `LogOutputChannel` enables better log granularity and can be filtered by level (info, warn, error).\\n- Be sure your extension's `engines.vscode` in `package.json` is set to a VS Code version that supports `LogOutputChannel` (\\u003e=1.56.0).\\n\\n## Further Reference\\n- [VS Code API Output Channels](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#window.createOutputChannel)\\n- [vscode-languageclient Changelog](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/blob/main/client/CHANGELOG.md)\\n\\nIf you provide more details on your use-case (e.g., code, error messages, or specific goals), I can offer more targeted help!\",\n    \"annotations\": null\n  },\n  \"bing_searches\": null,\n  \"annotations\": null\n}"}]},"toolTelemetry":{}},"id":"94835949-dd22-44b7-b362-845ce45727c5","timestamp":"2026-06-21T20:06:18.777Z","parentId":"24158593-b255-4bb0-bd93-72fe383225ce"}

Previously, these may have been synchronous/void, but now, the async nature is explicit to better reflect actual message delivery over the transport layer. As a result:\\n- If you are not awaiting the promise or handling it, you might get \\\"floating promise\\\" lint warnings or similar static analysis issues in your code.\\n- You may need to update your extensions or code to either `await` or deliberately handle these promises to avoid unhandled promise warnings or linter errors.\\n\\n**Summary of breaking change:**\\n- **Breaking**: All `sendNotification` methods now return a promise (instead of void), to better model the asynchronous nature of message writing to the transport. Unhandled (floating) promises may be flagged by tooling or linters【3:8†source】.\\n\\nIf you want more granular detail on other changes, the [changelog from the main repo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/blob/main/ChangeLog.md) details the full list of updates and any additional breaking changes for each release.\\n\\n**Recommendation:** If you maintain an extension using this version, `await` or `.catch()` notification method calls where appropriate.
